corpus.sequence_construction: Scored sequences are built over the strict sign set only (claim F033-C04): each inscription's signs are filtered to the 94 strict_sa_independent signs, order preserved as recorded. A sequence containing a non-strict sign is not scored as such; the strict signs it contains are scored in order (the sign population is what the freeze restricts).

robustness_lists.rule: Claim F033-C13: the next five published candidates per family, under the identical pipeline. Each family's list is drawn from that family's published sources as held in the record, ranked by corpus frequency (ties: lower sign number first), excluding the primary five. Alternant values in a source ('ay/ā') contribute their first-listed alternant; a trailing '-X' marks a sign-form modifier with no sound content in the source and is dropped, leaving the base word.

sanskrit_source_caveat: The Sanskrit sign map file (and its companion Rao-tradition map, not used here) describes itself as a synthetic reconstruction of the published Sanskrit decipherment traditions, built by this program (Phase-30) for testing those traditions fairly rather than from the traditions' own tables. The values are therefore cited to the underlying publications — Yajnadevam 2024 for the Sanskrit decipherment claim, Rao 1982 for the logographic tradition, Monier-Williams 1899 and Apte 1957 for the Sanskrit words — with the extraction file named as the held record the values were taken from. This caveat is part of the anchor freeze and is repeated in the outcome.
selection_rule_primary: A sign enters the primary candidate pool when all of these hold: (i) it is in the strict set; (ii) it occurs in the scored corpus; (iii) it carries a Dravidian value in the Parpola sign map (backend/glossa_lab/data/parpola_phonemes.json) at high or medium confidence, with no '?' and not marked 'uncertain'; (iv) it carries a Sanskrit value in the Sanskrit sign map (backend/glossa_lab/data/yajnadevam_phonemes_sanskrit.json), not marked 'uncertain'; (v) a Munda value for the sign's depicted referent can be cited from a published Munda source (below). The pool is ranked by frequency in the scored corpus, most frequent first, ties broken by the lower sign number. The first five form the primary list. Exactly nine signs met conditions (i)-(iv); all nine also met (v) or are recorded below with the reason they did not.

strict_set.source: backend/reports/INDUS_FINAL_ANCHORS.json, entries whose Spec 029 Phase H validation_status field equals 'strict_sa_independent'

unit_decomposition_rule: A published value becomes a sequence of sound units mechanically: lower-case the value; fold marked letters to their base letters (ā→a, ī→i, ū→u, ē→e, ō→o, ṭ→t, ḍ→d, ṇ→n, ṅ→n, ñ→n, ś→s, ṣ→s, ḷ→l, and the capital markers T, N, L in the Parpola map's ASCII spellings likewise); drop apostrophes (they mark a checked consonant in the Santali dictionary's spelling; the consonant itself is kept); where a source lists alternants separated by '/', take the first; drop a trailing '-X' sign-form modifier marker; then read the result one character at a time — each character is one unit. The 'units' arrays above are the result of this rule, computed and frozen here.
what_this_is: The two anchor lists the frozen Spec 033 contract requires (claims F033-C06 and F033-C13), written down as cited data — sign, published value, source — before any score was computed. Nothing in this file was chosen after seeing a score; the selection rules below are mechanical and are stated in full so anyone can re-derive the lists from the same sources.
